topic: You are looking at the past
claim: Light takes time to travel, so the Sun you see is about 8 minutes old and everything in the sky is seen as it was.

beats.caption: This light is 8 minutes old
beats.vo: The Sun you see is eight minutes old.

beats.caption: 93 million miles at light speed
beats.vo: The Sun is about ninety-three million miles away. Even light, the fastest thing there is, needs about eight minutes and twenty seconds to make that trip.

beats.caption: You see the Sun as it was
beats.vo: So you never see the Sun as it is right now. You see it as it was eight minutes ago. If it vanished this second, it would keep shining in our sky for eight more minutes.

beats.caption: Looking up = looking back
beats.vo: The Moon you see is about a second old. Most stars? Years, even thousands of years. Every time you look up, you're looking back in time.
